title: Featured snippets and direct answers
summary: Google describes featured snippets as special boxes where the format of a regular search result is reversed. Google's systems decide whether a page makes a good one; when asked whether you can mark a page as one, Google answers "You can't." Google gives no exact minimum length. A click goes to the section of the page shown. To opt out, nosnippet blocks all snippets including featured ones, data-nosnippet keeps marked text out, and Google says a shorter max-snippet makes a featured snippet less likely, without a guarantee that they stop.
actions: Audit templates for nosnippet, max-snippet and data-nosnippet that block snippets unintentionally.
Do not hunt for markup 'for featured snippets'; Google answers 'You can't' to marking a page as one.
Use data-nosnippet for specific text you want kept out of snippets.
Write clear, self-contained answers under descriptive headings (practitioner inference).

myths.myth: You can mark up a page to become a featured snippet.
myths.correction: Google answers "You can't."; its systems determine whether a page makes a good featured snippet.

myths.myth: A low max-snippet value reliably removes featured snippets.
myths.correction: Google says it makes them less likely but doesn't guarantee they stop.

items.prompt: What does Google call the special boxes where the format of a regular search result is reversed?
items.explanation: Google's featured snippets page defines them this way.

items.prompt: How does Google say a page becomes a featured snippet?
options: A. By adding featured-snippet markup to the page code
B. Google systems decide
C. By submitting the page through a Search Console request form
D. By paying Google for the featured position
items.explanation: Correct: Google systems determine whether a page would make a good featured snippet. Wrong: 'adding featured-snippet markup' - asked whether you can mark a page as one, Google answers "You can't." 'Search Console request form' - no such route is described. 'Paying' - not described; Google's systems decide.

items.prompt: True or false: Google publishes an exact minimum text length required to appear as a featured snippet.
items.explanation: Google says it does not provide an exact minimum length.

items.prompt: When a user clicks a featured snippet, Google says it takes them directly to what part of the page?
items.explanation: Google says clicking takes the user directly to the section of the page that appeared in the featured snippet.

items.prompt: A colleague says 'Setting max-snippet low guarantees featured snippets stop.' Which correction is best?
options: A. max-snippet has no effect whatsoever on featured snippets
B. Only nosnippet can ever change how snippets appear
C. Shorter settings make it less likely, with no guarantee
D. It forces featured snippets to appear for the page
items.explanation: Correct: Google says the shorter the max-snippet setting, the less likely the page will appear as a featured snippet, and that a low setting doesn't guarantee they stop. Wrong: 'no effect whatsoever' - Google says it makes it less likely. 'Only nosnippet can change snippets' - data-nosnippet and max-snippet also exist. 'It forces featured snippets to appear' - the opposite.

items.prompt: Which statement is NOT supported by the saved sources?
options: A. Text marked data-nosnippet won't appear in featured snippets
B. Featured snippets appear only if enough text can be shown
C. max-snippet 0 is equivalent to nosnippet
D. FAQ schema is required for a page to be eligible for featured snippets
items.explanation: Supported: data-nosnippet text won't appear in featured snippets (A); featured snippets appear only if enough text can be shown (B); max-snippet 0 equals nosnippet (C). Unsupported: D - no saved quote says FAQ schema is required for eligibility; when asked whether you can mark a page as one, Google answers "You can't.".

items.prompt: Hypothetical page: a pricing FAQ. The owner wants one paragraph kept out of featured and regular snippets while the rest stays eligible. Which HTML attribute does Google document for this?
items.explanation: Google says text marked by data-nosnippet won't appear in featured snippets or regular snippets.

items.prompt: A team plans: 'Wrap the key answer in data-nosnippet so it becomes our featured snippet.' What is the error?
options: A. data-nosnippet keeps text out of snippets, the opposite
B. data-nosnippet has been deprecated and Google ignores it now
C. Featured snippets never use any text from the page
D. data-nosnippet only applies to images and not to text
items.explanation: Correct: data-nosnippet does the opposite, keeping text out of snippets. Wrong: 'data-nosnippet is deprecated' - Google documents it. 'Featured snippets use no text' - they use text. 'It only works on images' - it marks text.

items.prompt: Hypothetical site: a recipe blog. Symptom: pages lost featured snippets and AI feature links after a plugin update. Evidence: (1) a site-wide robots meta tag now says nosnippet; (2) Google says nosnippet is the way to block all snippets including featured snippets; (3) Google says nosnippet also prevents use as direct input for AI Overviews and AI Mode. Question: what is the best action?
options: A. Add FAQ schema to each recipe page and wait
B. Remove the site-wide nosnippet
C. Set max-snippet to 0 on every recipe page
D. Noindex the recipe pages and resubmit the sitemap
items.explanation: Correct: remove the site-wide nosnippet if snippet appearance is wanted. Wrong: 'Add FAQ schema' - not a stated fix. 'Set max-snippet to 0' - equals nosnippet. 'Noindex the pages' - removes them from results.

items.prompt: Hypothetical site: a law firm. Symptom: it wants one disclaimer paragraph kept out of snippets, while the rest of the page stays eligible as a supporting link in AI Overviews and AI Mode. Evidence: (1) the page is indexed; (2) Google says nosnippet applies to all forms of search results and also prevents the content being used as direct input for AI Overviews and AI Mode; (3) Google says a supporting-link page must be indexed and eligible to be shown with a snippet; (4) data-nosnippet applies only to the marked text. Question: which action fits?
options: A. Add nosnippet to the whole page so nothing is shown
B. Add noindex to the whole page so it leaves results
C. Wrap only the disclaimer paragraph in data-nosnippet
D. Set max-snippet to 0 for the page as a whole
items.explanation: Correct: wrap only the paragraph in data-nosnippet, so the rest of the page can still be shown with a snippet and stay eligible. Wrong: nosnippet on the page blocks all snippets and AI input, ending the eligibility the firm wants to keep. noindex removes the page. max-snippet 0 is equivalent to nosnippet, so it has the same cost. The trade-off is that the disclaimer text itself will not appear in snippets.
